Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript, production marketing site for a VPS/game-server/web-hosting company, nxeon.cloud). This is a RESEARCH AND PREPARATION task, not an execution task — you will produce a report, draft copy, and (only for the specific on-site technical items below) real code changes in an isolated worktree. You will NOT create any external accounts, submit any real directory listings, or send any real outreach emails — those require the owner's review and action, not yours.

## Context

Real Search Console data just confirmed the core SEO bottleneck: the domain is ~5 weeks old with essentially zero backlink authority, so even indexed, well-written pages rank on page 7-8+ of Google for commercial terms (e.g. "cheap vps singapore" at position 79). More content won't fix this — off-page authority (backlinks, citations, directory presence) is the actual lever needed, alongside the content that already exists (346 blog posts, comparison pages like `/vps-vs-digitalocean`, free tools at `/tools/*` — check `app/tools/` or similar for the exact list: password generator, subnet calculator, port checker, etc. — these are read-only free utilities usable by anyone, a classic "linkable asset" for earning backlinks from "best free X tools" roundup articles).

## What to produce

### 1. Directory/listing research (report only, no signups)
Compile a prioritized list of legitimate, relevant directories and listing sites for a VPS/game-server/web-hosting business: think G2, Capterra, AlternativeTo, Product Hunt, SourceForge, StackShare, Slant, GetApp, TrustRadius, HostAdvice, WebHostingTalk, and hosting-specific comparison/review sites. For each: signup URL, whether it's free or paid, what's required (business verification, minimum reviews, etc.), and how much realistic SEO/referral value it likely has for a young hosting company (be honest about low-value ones — don't pad the list with directories that provide no real link equity, e.g. some are nofollow-only or have near-zero traffic). Use WebSearch to verify these are real, currently-operating sites with current requirements — do not rely on training-data memory for URLs/requirements, directory sites change frequently. For each directory in your final shortlist (aim for 10-15 genuinely worthwhile ones), draft the actual listing description copy (company blurb, feature bullets) ready to paste in, matching Nxeon's actual real feature set — read `app/page.tsx`/`app/(marketing)/features/page.tsx` and similar to ground the copy in real, accurate claims (NVMe VPS, DDoS protection, one-click game server deploys, etc. — verify against actual site copy, don't invent features).

### 2. Linkable-asset outreach research (report only, no emails sent)
Find the free tools pages in this codebase (likely `app/tools/**` or `app/(marketing)/tools/**` — locate them yourself) and use WebSearch to find 10-20 REAL, currently-published articles/roundup lists that already reference similar free tools (e.g. "best free subnet calculators", "free password generator tools", "best network diagnostic tools online") where Nxeon's equivalent tool could reasonably be added as a suggestion. For each: the article URL, the site's apparent authority/relevance, and a short, genuinely useful (not spammy) draft outreach email suggesting the addition — specific to that article's actual content, not a generic template blasted at all of them.

### 3. On-site technical trust signals — THESE you should actually implement in code
Work in an isolated worktree for this part only: `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-seo-trust-signals -b feature/seo-trust-signals` from /opt/nxeon (symlink node_modules/.env, never `git add -A`). Check whether these exist already before adding (don't duplicate):
- **Organization/LocalBusiness JSON-LD structured data** on the homepage and/or a dedicated `/about` or contact context — real schema.org markup search engines use for knowledge-panel/trust signals. Ground every field in real, verifiable info already on the site (don't invent an address/phone number that doesn't exist elsewhere in the codebase — if Nxeon doesn't publish a physical address anywhere, use `Organization` schema without a fabricated `address`, not `LocalBusiness` which requires one).
- **Review/rating schema** if the site already displays real review counts/ratings anywhere (the homepage mentions "4.9 on Trustpilot (312)" per earlier session context — verify this is real, currently-accurate data before marking it up, then add proper `AggregateRating`/`Review` JSON-LD if it's genuine and not already marked up).
- **Sitemap/robots.txt sanity check** — already confirmed working today (346 blog URLs present, robots.txt allows crawling), just do a final check that nothing regressed and that the new location pages (being built by a parallel agent, don't touch that work) will be picked up.
- Anything else genuinely low-risk, verifiably-true, and standard SEO technical hygiene you find missing — but do NOT fabricate content/data to make schema markup "richer." Under-filled-but-honest schema beats fabricated-but-complete schema.

## What NOT to do

- Do not create accounts anywhere, submit real listings, or send real emails.
- Do not touch location-pages, custom-server-plans, PayPal, Namecheap, or board-processing work — separate agents in parallel, different worktrees.
- Do not invent facts (addresses, phone numbers, review counts, feature claims) not already verifiably true elsewhere in this codebase or on the live site.

## Verification (for the code portion only)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npm test` — no new failures beyond the current 34 pre-existing baseline.

## Report format

Three clearly separated sections matching the three numbered tasks above. Section 1 and 2 are pure research/drafts (markdown tables/lists in your final report text, no files needed unless you think a saved draft doc is more useful — your call). Section 3: files created/modified, verification results, worktree path/branch name.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
